CURLING VISION / GEOMETRY EXPERIMENT

Put the ice back in proportion.

New: stone-body localization using this camera geometry →

The known house dimensions turn a camera view into a metric ice plane. This experiment rectifies every frame of a 90-second video and checks whether the painted rings agree with the geometry.

This is a top-down transformation of the ice, not a reconstructed overhead camera. Stones, handles and people rise above the ice, so they stretch in this view. Their visible tops still do not establish their ground positions.

Clear reference image

The refinement uses many points around the outer and middle rings. The inner ring is excluded; one quarter of outer/middle angular samples is also excluded. Four ring/line intersections anchor orientation.

Before / after, with evidence kept out of fitting

CheckBeforeAfter

All values are RMSE in centimetres for the selected camera. Ring checks measure radial alignment, not full two-dimensional position. Clicked points measure 2D position at four inner-ring intersections and the tee. The same AI selected the initial landmarks; neighbouring boundary samples are correlated.

What is verified through the video?

A new image-based ring check runs at every absolute registration. Between those checks, forward/backward optical flow must remain consistent across a spread of ice features. “Supported” is an engineering acceptance gate, not a calibrated probability.

Other timestamps and known camera-movement tests →

How this fits into the project.

1. Fit metric geometry

Known radii + reference ring boundaries → image-to-ice homography.

2. Follow the camera

Absolute feature registration + per-frame optical flow → current projection.

3. Verify and rectify

Ring evidence and motion checks → metric pixels, or an unavailable result.

4. Estimate stone footprints

Still unresolved. Height-aware localization must precede accurate board-state reconstruction.

Assumptions, limitations and reproducibility

The recording has two fixed camera panels and known manually initialized reference images. Ring radii are nominal 1.829, 1.219 and 0.610 metres. Lens distortion is not estimated. The mapping is supported around the house; accuracy farther along the sheet is not established. Rotation follows the view-local tee and centre lines; these cameras are not fused into one game coordinate system.

The output uses a planar homography; it does not claim a uniquely recovered 3D camera pose. Generic uploads still use the older index. Accurate stone footprints, arbitrary-video calibration, shot segmentation and scoring are unfinished.
